Inferred: the authors link AIMP2 depletion to cell death in the developing brain; that reduced translation is the step in between is the working hypothesis rather than a tested link.
Proposed for the synthetase leukodystrophies as a group: reduced translation capacity leads to insufficient myelin deposition in the developing brain. Not tested for AIMP2.
Cell death and brain atrophy were reported together in the zebrafish model.
Inferred: small head size accompanies brain atrophy in these patients; microcephaly is already present at birth in some, so reduced brain growth before birth likely contributes as well.

nodes.description: Delayed and deficient myelination with white matter abnormality on MRI. In the one serially imaged patient, white matter signal was normal at 5 days, myelination was mildly delayed at 2 months, and white matter loss with periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintensity (which the authors thought might be gliosis) was present at 7 months. Published MRI descriptions emphasise atrophy more than a pure hypomyelination pattern, as in the AIMP1-related HLD3, and how much of the white matter change is primary myelin deficit rather than loss secondary to neuronal degeneration is not settled.
